cases.migration_note: Both v2 and the public Object Query route return an empty list for no results; no error handling change is needed for the not-found case on a list operation.
cases.public_oq: A filtered list returns an empty data array when no records match; it does not return 404.
cases.v2: A list operation returns an empty data array when no records match; it does not return 404.

cases.migration_note: The public invoice items list requires a filter; v2 allowed an unfiltered call. Always supply at least one filter (for example filter[]=invoiceid.EQ:<id>). Both routes return 400 for invalid filter keys or values; the error body shape changes from the v2 structure to { error: { code, message } }. Update filter expressions to use the public OQ field names.
cases.public_oq: 400, body { error: { code: integer, message: string } } (observed). An unfiltered call returns 500 with message 'A filter is required to query object: invoiceitem'. Always supply at least one filter.
cases.v2: 400, type bad_request, code invalid_parameter, parameter filter[]; body includes the invalid field name or value.

cases.migration_note: Both v2 and the public Object Query route use page size bounds 1-99. Rename page_size to pageSize; a value from 1 to 99 carries over unchanged, and a literal outside 1 to 99 is clamped to the nearest bound and reported. An invalid cursor returns 500 instead of 400 on the public route (observed behavior).
cases.public_oq: 400, body { error: { code: integer, message: string } } (observed); pageSize bounds: 1-99 (default 10). An invalid cursor returns 500 { errors: [{ message: ... }] } (observed).
cases.v2: 400, type bad_request, errors[0].parameter page_size; raised by request-schema validation when page_size is outside 1-99 or the cursor is malformed

cases.migration_note: v2 does not return 400 for non-hex ID values in list filter parameters; the list returns no matching rows. The public route behaves the same way for identifier filters. No error-handling change is needed.
cases.public_oq: not documented; a list filtered by a non-matching id returns 200 with an empty data array (observed).
cases.v2: v2 list filters do not validate identifier format; a filter with a non-hex ID value is passed through and returns an empty data array.

cases.migration_note: The public route returns 400 for a missing token and 401 for an invalid token, not always 401 as v2 did. Ensure your OAuth bearer token is present and valid, and that the requesting user has permission to read invoice items.
cases.public_oq: A missing bearer token returns 400 { message: 'No bearer token' }; an invalid token returns 401 { message: 'Authentication error' }; a 403 is returned for permission errors (observed).
cases.v2: 401, type unauthorized, empty errors array when the bearer token is missing or invalid.

cases.migration_note: The retryable flag in the v2 response body must not be used as a retry signal; v2 always sets it to false for Object Query errors. Implement retry logic based on the HTTP status code; retry on 429 and 5xx and respect any Retry-After header.
cases.public_oq: not documented; a 429 response is not documented on this route. Keep retrying on 429 and 5xx as you do today.
cases.v2: 500, type internal_server_error, retryable false; upstream Object Query failures produce a v2 500 response with retryable set to false

route.body: { error: { code: integer, message: string } } for 400 and 404 errors (observed); a missing bearer token returns 400 { message: 'No bearer token' }; an invalid token returns 401 { message: 'Authentication error' }; an invalid cursor returns 500 { errors: [{ message: ... }] } (observed).

limitation.note: The public API behaves differently from v2 here. The public API behaves differently from v2 here. v2 narrows the upstream data fetch to only the requested fields before sending the query; the public OQ REST fields[] parameter narrows only the response output. Supply invoiceitem.fields[] with public OQ field names to project the response. For parity with v2 upstream data fetch narrowing, accept that the public REST fields[] parameter controls only the response output projection, not the upstream data retrieval. Object Query GraphQL (public, undocumented; evidence is source-observed) can provide parity; see the shared GraphQL parity reference entry GP-7.

A name the API does not know (for example invoice_item.fields[]) is silently ignored and the full record is returned. Output field order is not preserved.

For each row of `data[]` in the successful JSON response, build the `custom_fields` object. Always build the object: it is `{}` when the row has no custom fields. Use the `customFields` array when the row has one, otherwise the `custom_fields` array; turn each `{key, value, type}` entry into `key: value` (when a key appears more than once, the last entry wins). Then convert `long` and `number` values to numbers, convert `boolean` values to true or false, and leave other types unchanged; null values stay null. If the row has neither array, collect every property whose name ends in `__c` into the object; an empty array gives `{}` and the `__c` properties are then not used. Include `custom_fields` only when it was requested.

unsupported.note: The public APIs do not accept this header. The v2 API accepted the x-custom-auth and zuora-cache-enabled request headers; neither header has a public equivalent. The invoice items list route did not wire a cache handler, so zuora-cache-enabled had no effect on this operation. The public APIs authenticate via a bearer token in the Authorization header and optionally accept zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to an entity and zuora-track-id for request tracing. Send the OAuth bearer token in the Authorization header. Pass zuora-entity-ids to scope the request to a specific entity, or zuora-track-id for request tracing. Do not send zuora-cache-enabled; the public APIs have no such header. No vetted GraphQL example is available.
